name: Lying and Deceit

counsel.text: The heart and tongue should go together, as the dial goes exactly with the sun. To speak fair to one's face, and not to mean what one speaks, is no better than a lie.
counsel.author: Thomas Watson
counsel.source: A Body of Divinity, the truth of God

counsel.text: If ever thou wilt mortify thy corruptions, thou must tie up thy conscience to the law, shut it from all shifts and exceptions, until it owns its guilt with a clear and thorough apprehension; so that thence, as David speaks, thy "iniquity may ever be before thee."
counsel.author: John Owen
counsel.source: Of the Mortification of Sin in Believers, ch. 11

counsel.text: Lying is a sin that does not go alone; it ushers in other sins. Absalom told his father a lie, when he said that he was going to pay his vow at Hebron, and this was a preface to his treason.
counsel.author: Thomas Watson
counsel.source: The Ten Commandments, the ninth commandment

counsel.text: It is the Spirit alone that can do, that doth, this work to the purpose. And this is the first thing that the Spirit doth in order to the mortification of any lust whatever, -- it convinces the soul of all the evil of it, cuts off all its pleas, discovers all its deceits, stops all its evasions, answers its pretences, makes the soul own its abomination, and lie down under the sense of it.
counsel.author: John Owen
counsel.source: Of the Mortification of Sin in Believers, ch. 14

counsel.text: When thou speakest, let thy word be as authentic as thy oath. Imitate God, who is the pattern of truth.
counsel.author: Thomas Watson
counsel.source: The Ten Commandments, the ninth commandment

counsel.text: By a lie in our words we deny the truth; by a lie in our profession we disgrace it.
counsel.author: Thomas Watson
counsel.source: A Body of Divinity, the truth of God

prayers.title: A prayer of confession
prayers.text: Father, I have lied. I covered myself, I deceived others, and I acted as if you did not see. But nothing is hidden from you, and I do not want to hide any longer. I confess it plainly. You are the God of truth, and you have promised to forgive and cleanse all who confess their sins. I trust in the blood of Jesus Christ, my Advocate with you, who is himself the truth. Forgive me for his sake. Holy Spirit, make me hate deceit, give me courage to set things right with those I misled, and make me true in my heart. Amen.

prayers.title: When a lie is on my lips
prayers.text: Lord Jesus, I am about to bend the truth to protect myself. You are the truth, and I belong to you. I would rather be humbled before others than be false before you. Give me courage to say what is so, plainly and kindly, and to trust you with whatever follows. Holy Spirit, quiet my fear of what people will think of me. Let my words mean exactly what they say. Amen.

prayers.title: For a true heart
prayers.text: Father, I want to look good more than I want to be good. Take away my pretending and my half-truths. You see me as I am, and in Christ you have not turned me away, so I have no need to hide from you or from anyone. Holy Spirit, show me my own deceits before I tell them. Make me the same person in private as I am in public, and make my yes and my no honest. Amen.

examinationQuestions: When you were tempted to shade the truth today, what were you afraid of: blame, losing face, or losing something you wanted?
Have you been trusting a lie to protect you more than you have trusted God to keep you?
Did you leave anyone with a false picture today, through silence, a half-truth, or exaggeration?
Is there a lie you have told that still stands? What would it take to set it right?
Are you living one way before others and another way before God?
Are you being honest with yourself about this sin, or are you making excuses for it?
fleeActions: Stop before you answer. Then say only what is true, even if your answer is short.
If you have just told a lie, go back now and correct it. Say plainly what you said and what is really true.
Do not send the message or sign the form until every word in it is true.
Tell a brother or sister in your church about the lie you are tempted to keep, so that it is brought into the light.
Open your Bible to Psalm 32, read it, and confess the matter to God out loud.
Write down what you fear will happen if you tell the truth, then pray and give that fear to God.

afterFallReadings.text: Christ by his intercession answers all bills of indictment brought in against the elect. Do what they can, sin, and then Satan, accuses believers to God, and conscience accuses them to themselves; but Christ, by his intercession, answers all these accusations.
afterFallReadings.author: Thomas Watson
afterFallReadings.source: A Body of Divinity, Christ's priestly office
